aria: Animated recap of the 76ers' 121 to 116 win at Orlando: VJ Edgecombe's go-ahead 3-pointer from LeBron James with 1:36 left, quarter-by-quarter scoring after a 17-point first-quarter deficit, Joel Embiid's 26 points and 7 assists, the top scorers, how Philadelphia won, and Saturday's game against Milwaukee.
notes: Box score from the Philadelphia 76ers' 121–116 win over the Orlando Magic at the Kia Center on Nov 18, 2026, from the CBS Sports box score, checked against the Covers box score and NBA House, with game details from the Associated Press (via Yahoo Sports), GMA News and Yardbarker. All 121 Philadelphia points and all 116 Orlando points are accounted for, and the quarter scores add up to both totals: Orlando 40–27 after one, 69–64 at the half, 97–92 after three. Field goals (42 of 81 to 44 of 84), threes (14 of 35 to 19 of 37), free throws (23 of 26 to 9 of 17), rebounds (38–37) and assists (27–31) are from the box score; points in the paint (40–46) and the biggest leads (Orlando 17, Philadelphia 8) are from Covers. Joel Embiid's free throws are 12 of 14 in all three box scores (AP has 12 of 15). Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Wednesday's games.

Orlando went up 36–19 late in the first quarter on a 27–12 run capped by Franz Wagner's driving layup and led for 41 minutes (GMA; AP; CBS play-by-play). Walker's 3-pointer with 5:09 left gave Philadelphia its first lead since 5–3 (GMA). Jalen Suggs' three put Orlando up 112–111 with 2:01 left, then VJ Edgecombe's 3-pointer on a no-look pass from LeBron James made it 114–112 with 1:36 left (AP; CBS play-by-play; Yardbarker). Anfernee Simons' three with 15 seconds left made it 119–113 (GMA; CBS play-by-play). Edgecombe scored a season-high 24, 13 of them in the fourth (AP). Tyrese Maxey was a late scratch with a foot injury, Jaylen Brown (hamstring) also sat, and Simons made his first start of the season (AP; GMA). It was Philadelphia's fourth straight win and, at 13–3, its best start in 26 years (AP; GMA). The 76ers host Milwaukee on Saturday (Yardbarker).

The play of the game is an original illustration of VJ Edgecombe's 28-foot 3-pointer with 1:36 left that put Philadelphia ahead 114–112 for good (AP gives the clock, the score and James' no-look pass; Yardbarker the distance). The recaps don't describe the shot further, so it is drawn as the template's plain pull-up from beyond the arc. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Philadelphia 76ers or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Edgecombe's listed 6-foot-4 and 190 pounds (Wikipedia), with his arms scaled to the 6-foot-7½ wingspan reported by NBC Sports Philadelphia, in Philadelphia's road colors with No. 77 (Wikipedia). He has no approved look on file yet, so he is drawn in the kit with the default skin tone. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
